title: Charles Hémard de Denonville, cardinal de Mâcon, Rome and Orvieto to Anne de Montmorency, 1536-37 (BnF fr. 3053; DECODE R4233-R4248)

transcription.notes: Line count is of cipher lines, not tokens; the readings file gives aliases per line.
About 250 cipher lines; 66 transcribed (P2, P3, P5, P6).
Two letters and a postscript in one record; read in passages (R4239.md P2-P15, R4239b.md P16-P30).

documents.date: 1 Sept 1536 (letter 2); letter 1 of the same days

transcription.notes: Two letters in one record, about 57 and 26 cipher lines.
A second, different fr. 3053 cipher; not Mâcon's key.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on digit-like graphic signs, one sign per letter, with doubled-letter signs, nulls and three two-digit code groups.
system.sibling_key: 'Mascon's cipher' as reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from this volume and tabulated by G. Lasry (2023) for BnF fr. 3071 f. 9; used here, with corrections.
system.notes: Code groups 20 = l'Empereur, 30 = pape, 40 = roy, and no others in any of the eight records. The barred-cross family of signs reads F, P, O, U, V and D in the same hand and is separable only by context; the big curly X is Q/U, not N, contrary to the working table. The f. 85 record (R4248) uses a second, unrelated fr. 3053 cipher.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some passages in the volume itself, and a full clear decipherment of the f. 85 cipher on f. 86. No printed or online plaintext: Tomokiyo and Lasry publish the key only.

conditions.human_role: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images

solution.what: Checked Tomokiyo's francis.htm, Lasry's GL.htm, DECODE's sixteen fr. 3053 records and the Dodieu edition table for a published decipherment
Identified the catalogue's 'unknown sender' as the cardinal de Mâcon from Tomokiyo's description of the volume and from the clear signatures on R4239, R4240 and R4247
Fetched the sixteen record pages and the images of the eight target records from DECODE with the stored cookie
Applied 'Mascon's cipher' (macon_key.md, built in gramont1529 from Lasry's and Tomokiyo's tables) to the cipher lines
Glyph-level transcription of the cipher passages of all eight records by reading agents, one or two records at a time
Six contemporary marginal or interlinear decipherments found in the volume; three agree with the independent decoding word for word
Corrected the working table from a glossed line ('quant au faict de florence'): the big curly X is Q/U, not N, and the QUE group is written three ways
Read R4240 (~85%), R4247 letter 1 (~80%), R4238 (~65%), R4233 (~60%), passages of R4235 and R4239, and 66 lines of R4234
Found that the f. 85 cipher (R4248) is not Mâcon's but a second fr. 3053 cipher, deciphered in clear at the time on f. 86, and read the passage from that

gaps.detail: untouched; needs page-at-a-time passes with the known key

gaps.item: residue of the read passages (R4233 ~40%, R4234 P2-P6 ~30%, R4238 ~35%, R4240 ~15%, R4247 letter 1 ~20%)
gaps.detail: barred-cross family (ǂ, £, long ƒ) reads F/P/O/U/V/D within a line, separable only by context

outcome.notes: Seven records read in part, one (R4248) resolved by the contemporary decipherment on the next leaf. The limit is the hand and the ambiguous barred-cross signs, not the cryptanalysis: the key was known before the attempt. R4234 (~250 cipher lines) is three quarters unread.
